rule: Skill-primer drills are done at RIR 4 (<= ~70% effort, fresh, stop when mechanics degrade)
summary: Branscheidt 2019 (lab experiments) found that practising a skill while muscles are fatigued impaired learning on later days, not just performance on the day. That supports practising technique fresh and far from failure. A 2026 RCT in which fatigue came from whole-body cardio found no learning cost in a non-fatigued limb, so the effect may depend on local muscle fatigue; either way, a low-effort, fresh primer costs nothing. RIR 4 is a sensible proxy, though RIR has little meaning for body-position drills, where 'stop when mechanics degrade' is the operative rule.

sources.note: Branscheidt 2019 eLife: muscle fatigue during practice impaired motor-skill learning on later non-fatigued days
de Morais 2026, n=60: cardio-induced fatigue before practice did not impair learning in a non-fatigued limb
Nagatani 2026: fatigue within sets changes power-clean bar path; low-fatigue structures preserve technique
